text:
maria: noticing a spike in token auth failures, quota engine is returning 429s for some premium routes

sam: saw that, paging dashboards show a token surge from a single client id ~10:12 UTC, throttles firing

jordan: can we do a soft-override to let premium routes through while we investigate? we should avoid app downtime for paying customers

maria: proposal: gate is quota-v2. we can inject header `x-rw-override: quota-soft` at the gateway for route match `/api/v1/generate` and `/api/v1/chat` for requests with header `x-client-tier: enterprise`

devx: agree but need telemetry flag so we can count bypassed tokens separately. also set TTL on override = 15m and auto-expire

sam: +1 on TTL. also add a rate limit for the override itself to avoid someone blasting us by faking tier header

ops-bot: deploy requested by @maria: apply-gateway-override v1 to eng-gw-us-east (canary 10%)

maria: rolling canary 10% to start. config snippet below (apply with `gwctl patch`):

```yaml
- match: 
    path_prefix: "/api/v1"
    headers:
      x-client-tier: "enterprise"
  actions:
    - insert_header:
        name: "x-rw-override"
        value: "quota-soft"
    - telemetry_label: "soft-override-enterprise"
  ttl: 15m
```

jordan: logging config: we need `telemetry.soft_override=true` for these requests, and an alert if bypass rate > 50req/s

devx: updating dashboards: add a stacked series for bypassed_token_count and override_error_count. pin to top of the incident board

sam: can someone sanity-check fallback behavior? if quota system still rejects after header, we should mark as failed and revert quickly

maria: yes. fallback policy: after 3 consecutive rejects for same route+client, remove override for that client for 30m and create incident annotation

tay: oncanary now. seeing successful passes for canary traffic, telemetry shows soft_override label tagging requests

ops-bot: canary -> 10% success. change set id: cs_2026_2350004444_01

jordan: do we have a rollback plan? if error rate increases, script: `gwctl revert cs_2026_2350004444_01` to strip header injection and TTLs

sam: test plan to verify rollback: run synthetic load against enterprise token set and ensure 429s resume if revert executed

maria: manual hold for 5m, watch metrics. if bypass_error_rate > 1% or latency > 200ms, rollback immediately

devx: note for console: add a readout showing active overrides (name, scope, ttl, created_by) so SREs can triage quickly next time

tay: 5m in, metrics stable. soft_override pass rate 98%. no abnormal latency. leaving canary to ramp to 50%

ops-bot: ramping canary to 50% per @maria

sam: ramp looks good. telemetry shows small subset of clients still hitting rejects — opening follow-up to examine their auth tokens

maria: creating postmortem ticket and follow-up: investigate token issuer misconfig. will keep override until root cause found or 6h max

jordan: minor ask: please annotate the incident board with the `cs_2026_2350004444_01` change set and include who ran the revert step (if any)

devx: added dashboard widgets and an audit row for the override. assigned to @maria to close when done

maria: thanks team. leaving this thread open while we monitor. will update every 30m or on any rollback

tay: oof thanks — big props to the quick header-inject pattern, saved customers from a nasty outage :thumbsup:
